claims.text: Pt-Ni can be structured as nanoparticles with a Pt-rich shell and a Ni-rich core.
Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles can enhance HER catalytic activity relative to conventional pure Pt catalysts.
Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles can enhance HOR catalytic activity relative to conventional pure Pt catalysts.
Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles can provide greater durability during HER/HOR operation than pure Pt catalysts.
Pure Pt nanoparticles are conventionally used for HER and HOR applications.
Alloying in the Pt-Ni core-shell structure modifies the electronic structure of the Pt-rich surface.
The modified surface electronic structure produces an optimal hydrogen binding energy.
Incorporating Ni shifts the d-band center of the Pt surface.
The Ni-induced d-band-center shift adjusts hydrogen adsorption energy to a more favorable level for HER kinetics.
The Ni-induced d-band-center shift adjusts hydrogen adsorption energy to a more favorable level for HOR kinetics.
A Pt-rich shell protects the less noble Ni-rich core from dissolution.
Protection of Ni from dissolution enhances durability under electrochemical cycling.
Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles will exhibit lower HER/HOR overpotential than pure Pt nanoparticles.
Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles will exhibit higher HER/HOR current density than pure Pt nanoparticles.
Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles will retain performance better during long-term cycling than pure Pt nanoparticles.
The proposed activity and durability benefits are limited to acidic environments.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on particle size, synthesis conditions, and Pt:Ni ratio.
Performance in alkaline environments may differ from performance in acidic environments.
